name: KidCheck
shortDescription: A US children’s and youth check-in platform with attendance, guardian notifications, optional volunteer tools and printed labels.
suitableContexts: Churches needing a dedicated children’s check-in workflow

pricing.summary: KidCheck publishes US-dollar prices per check-in device: Starter $25, Plus $45 and Premier $60 monthly. Each has a published unlimited-device add-on and 90-day money-back guarantee.
pricing.trialDetails: KidCheck publishes a 90-day money-back guarantee rather than a free trial.

support: Setup, training and live support stated by supplier

editorial.assessment: KidCheck is a purpose-built check-in product with clear device-based pricing. UK churches should validate data-processing terms, hardware availability and their physical collection procedure; software alone cannot establish safe handovers or safeguarding practice.
bestFor: Churches wanting dedicated check-in rather than a wider ChMS module
strengths: Guardian accounts, check-out and notification features are stated
limitations: US-dollar plans and UK data terms need confirmation
Not a replacement for safeguarding policy or volunteer supervision

longForm.verdict: KidCheck is a focused option when the practical priority is children’s check-in and collection. Its value should be proven through a live rehearsal with parents, labels, devices and the people who actually lead children’s ministry.

decisionLens.heading: A check-in screen does not prove a safe handover.
decisionLens.text: Confirm who verifies collection, how exceptions are handled, where emergency details are held and what happens when a printer or network fails. These are church procedures supported by software, not responsibilities the software takes away.

sections.heading: Dedicated check-in workflow
sections.question: Will the team use it consistently at the door?
paragraphs: KidCheck publishes child and youth check-in, attendance, parent-maintained accounts, guardian notifications and check-out functions. Its pricing is based on edition and licensed check-in devices rather than attendance count.

Use a demo to practice normal and exceptional collection scenarios. Before processing live child data, obtain the supplier’s relevant privacy information and confirm how data can be exported, corrected and removed.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score. It is based on KidCheck’s official pricing and feature pages.
themes: Device and label workflow need testing in the church building.
Safeguarding depends on people and procedures as well as check-in technology.
userFeedback.caveat: Supplier security claims are not an independent safeguarding assessment or proof of UK GDPR suitability.

faq.question: How much does KidCheck cost?
faq.answer: Published prices are $25, $45 and $60 per month for one device across Starter, Plus and Premier, with an unlimited-device add-on for each.

faq.question: Does KidCheck offer a free trial?
faq.answer: Not confirmed. The supplier publishes a 90-day money-back guarantee and a free demo.

faq.question: Does KidCheck replace safeguarding procedures?
faq.answer: No. It can support check-in and collection records, but the church remains responsible for its safeguarding policies, supervision and handover process.
